messages.subject: saturated model with multiple groups
parts:
I'm trying to run a saturated model for 2 groups with no constraints (just a baseline, for a teaching example). I have 8 variables: 

gender.sat <-  'V1 ~~ V2 + V3 + V4 + V5 + V6 + V7 + V8
V2 ~~ V3 + V4 + V5 + V6 + V7 + V8
V3 ~~ V4 + V5 + V6 + V7 + V8
V4 ~~ V5 + V6 + V7 + V8
V5 ~~ V6 + V7 + V8
V6 ~~ V7 + V8
V7 ~~ V8'

Running the 2 groups separately works just fine, e.g.:
> M5.fitF <- cfa(gender.sat, sample.cov = cov.F, sample.mean =  mean.F, sample.nobs = 397, meanstructure = TRUE)

But if I run it as a multiple group model I get no convergence: 
> M5.fit <- cfa(gender.sat, sample.cov = gender.cov, sample.mean = gender.mean, sample.nobs = list(397, 282), meanstructure = TRUE)
 (gender.cov and gender.mean are lists -- syntax attached, and note that I have no problem running an actual multiple group cfa model with this input)

I get: 
Warning message:
In lavaan(model = gender.sat, meanstructure = TRUE, sample.cov = gender.cov, : 
    lavaan WARNING: model has NOT converged!
> 
the output doesn't even give me df ("NA") but it appears to be trying to estimate all the right parameters (covariances, means, variances). Specifying fixed.x = FALSE doesn't help, nor does removing the meanstructure.  Any idea what I'm doing wrong? 

Thanks much! 
Mijke

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: saturated model with multiple groups
parts:
Could this be another case where a sharp difference in the scale of variances is the problem?  You have one variable whose standard deviation is about 30 and others whose standard deviations are less than 1.  the standard deviations range by a factor of almost 100 to 1, so variances would range by a factor of almost 10,000 to 1.  Many or most SEM packages have problems in such cases.  (The Mplus people, for example, specifically warn about it.). Divide that variable by 10 and try again.
--Ed Rigdon

Thanks much! You're right-- it runs fine without V2 in the model. It hadn't occurred to me that drastically different variances could affect estimation of a saturated model (especially when the two groups run just fine separately, and the structured models I've fit on these data haven't run into problems either). 

Best,
Mijke

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: saturated model with multiple groups
parts:
On 11/10/2013 03:53 PM, Edward Rigdon wrote:
> Could this be another case where a sharp difference in the scale of
> variances is the problem?

Yes. The current version of lavaan (0.5-14) is still rather sensitive to
(rather large: ratio largest/smallest > 1000) scale differences. I think
I have found a way to circumvent this (rescale internally using the
Delta matrices), but I still have to implement this.

But a warning should be in order. lavaan would have given you a warning
if full data was supplied, but not (yet) if sample statistics are
provided. I will fix this.

BTW, to enter a correlation matrix + standard deviations, you can use
the 'getCov()' function:


tmp <- '
1
.1172 1
.1328 .1157 1
-.1267 -.1223 -.4295 1
-.1114 -.0477 -.3061 .3702 1
-.0091 -.0304 .0061 .1695 .1809 1
-.0368 -.0224 .0167 .0106 -.0151 -.3349 1
.1197 .0577 .1020 -.1178 -.1409 -.4151 .2635 1 '

cov.F <- getCov(tmp, sds = c(.36, 29.07, 1.34, .74, .89, 1.25, 1.23, 1.13))

(there is also an optional 'names' argument for providing variable names
other than V1, V2, ...)

Yves.
